Mongoose also says reducing it gives faster feedback on failed connections.

edits.new: `nearest` does not guarantee geographic proximity or the absolute lowest application latency. It admits eligible servers within the configured RTT window, so a server slower than the lowest-RTT candidate can still be selected when `localThresholdMS` is positive. To always select the lowest-RTT server, the spec says to use `nearest` without tag sets or maxStalenessSeconds and set `localThresholdMS` to zero. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/specifications/master/source/server-selection/server-selection.md

edits.old: As of 2026-10-22, the driver specification says single-threaded clients choose randomly within the latency window, while multithreaded or asynchronous clients choose two random candidates and select the one with the lower `operationCount`, which estimates in-flight work. The Kotlin coroutine guide documents this two-candidate rule. The Ruby, PyMongo, and Rust guides still describe a single random choice; the Ruby issue tracker says Ruby still uses shuffle-and-pick-first and has no `operationCount` tracking.
